ai.title: CLI bash command context unified for LLM
ai.summary: Refactored CLI to unify bash command context handling for the LLM. Manual commands executed via `/` or ghost mode are now consistently tracked in `pendingBashMessages` with an `addedToHistory` flag, and formatted into a `<user_terminal_commands>` block via `formatBashContextForPrompt` before sending to the model. This replaces the previous split logic where some commands were excluded from LLM context or handled via a separate `pendingToolResults` store. Scope covers `cli/src/chat.tsx`, `cli/src/commands/router.ts`, `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts`, `cli/src/state/chat-store.ts`, and `cli/src/utils/bash-messages.ts`. The `PendingToolResult` type and related store actions were removed in favor of the unified `PendingBashMessage` flow.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the chat (either with a slash or in ghost mode), the assistant now stores it in a single list with a flag saying whether it was already shown in the chat window, instead of keeping some commands in one place and others in a separate list. When you send your next message, the assistant bundles those stored commands and their outputs into one block it shows to the AI model, so the AI always has consistent context about what you just ran. This means fewer duplicated or missing command details in the conversation. Live today.

ai.title: Refine editor agent prompt and tool extraction
ai.summary: Updates `createCodeEditor` in `.agents/editor/editor.ts` to conditionally omit `<think>` instructions for `gpt-5` and explicitly forbid `set_output` usage. The `handleSteps` generator now extracts only `<codebuff_tool_call>` blocks from assistant text via regex, stripping commentary before yielding `STEP_TEXT`. This ensures cleaner tool execution and prevents output pollution from model reasoning traces.

eli5.text: When the writing assistant works through a task step by step, it now ignores any extra commentary or internal reasoning the model produces and only picks up the actual tool commands it was supposed to run, keeping the output cleaner. The assistant is also told more firmly that one particular shortcut should not be used, and a thinking prompt is skipped for one specific model version. These adjustments affect how the internal code-editing agent processes instructions and results, so anything built on top of that editor will see tidier, more predictable behavior starting today.

ai.title: BuffBench supports external Claude and Codex CLI agents
ai.summary: BuffBench evals now accept `external:claude` and `external:codex` agent identifiers to benchmark against Anthropic and OpenAI CLI tools. Implementation adds `ClaudeRunner` and `CodexRunner` classes in `evals/buffbench/runners/` that spawn CLI processes with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and parse `stream-json` output into internal `AgentStep` events. `run-buffbench.ts` updated with `parseAgentId` to route external types, while `agent-runner.ts` delegates execution to the new runner interface. Requires global installation of `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` or `@openai/codex` and respective API keys in environment.

eli5.text: BuffBench now lets you run Claude and Codex CLI tools alongside Codebuff agents to see which one performs better, requiring those CLI tools and their API keys to be installed globally. The system parses the external agents' JSON output into the same step-by-step format used by internal agents. If you use 'external:claude' or 'external:codex' as agent names, the tool spawns those external CLI processes with permission-skipping flags and tracks their actions for comparison. Errors get saved to files, but malformed tool calls don't.

ai.title: Buffbench runners pass API keys from process env
ai.summary: agent-runner.ts injects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY from process.env into the runner env for claude and codex agents. ClaudeRunner.ts drops the CLAUDE_CODE_KEY fallback that previously set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Affects evals/buffbench/agent-runner.ts and evals/buffbench/runners/claude.ts. Keys are added only when present in process.env, preserving existing env otherwise.

eli5.text: When the automated test system runs coding assistants (Claude or Codex) to evaluate their behavior, it now pulls your secret API keys directly from your computer's environment instead of relying on a fallback stored in a separate variable. This means if you have your Anthropic or OpenAI key set normally in your terminal session, the test runners will use that exact key rather than any leftover one from a different config variable. The system also stops copying an obsolete key-mapping that was previously used as a backup. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment for internal evaluation tooling and does not change anything for people simply using the assistants.

ai.title: Add image support to CLI
ai.summary: CLI now supports image attachment via /image command and clipboard paste. New utils handle image validation, dimension calculation, and terminal rendering (jimp, terminal-image). Chat store tracks pendingImages; router and command registry integrate image mode. Includes UI components for image blocks, cards, thumbnails, and input/pending banners.

eli5.text: You can now include images when chatting with the assistant in the command-line tool. Instead of only typing messages, you can attach a picture by running a command like /image path/to/photo.png, or by copying an image and pasting it directly into the terminal. The assistant sees the image alongside your text, and the interface shows a small preview of any picture you've added but not yet sent. This works today in the CLI, affects anyone using the command-line chat, and is live now.

ai.title: Revert agent runner key injection
ai.summary: Reverts commit "Update agent runners to use the appropriate key" in evals/buffbench/agent-runner.ts. Removed logic in runAgentOnCommit that explicitly copied ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY from process.env into the runner's env object. ClaudeRunner in evals/buffbench/runners/claude.ts now handles key resolution directly via CLAUDE_CODE_KEY fallback. Scope limited to internal buffbench evaluation runners.

eli5.text: The internal tool that runs automated coding tests for an AI assistant no longer passes along saved login credentials in a separate step before launching the assistant. Instead, the assistant now looks up its own credentials when it starts up, using a specific key as a backup if the main one isn't found. If you manage these automated tests, you might notice the credentials are handled a little later in the process than before, but the end result for any run is the same.

ai.title: Disable announcement banner in CLI chat-store
ai.summary: Set isAnnouncementVisible to false in initialState within cli/src/state/chat-store.ts. Hides the announcement banner by default for CLI sessions. Affects CLI state initialization only.

eli5.text: When you start a chat using the command-line tool, the announcement banner will no longer appear at the top of the screen. Previously, this banner was shown by default as part of the initial chat setup, but this change sets it to be hidden from the start. If you interact with the CLI chat, you won't see the banner unless it's specifically turned on later.

ai.title: Remove git-evals, migrate to buffbench
ai.summary: Deleted the deprecated `evals/git-evals` directory, consolidating evaluation logic into `evals/buffbench`. Imports in `gen-evals.ts` and `gen-repo-eval.ts` updated to reference local `setup-test-repo` and `pick-commits` modules within the new directory. Removed CLI entry point from `setup-test-repo.ts` and associated email reporting scripts. This change reduces internal code duplication and aligns the eval infrastructure with the current buffbench architecture.

eli5.text: The team deleted the old evaluation system and moved everything into the newer buffbench folder, so all the testing tools now live in one place instead of two. You would see the old git-evals folder is gone and the same files (setup-test-repo and pick-commits) now sit inside evals/buffbench. The standalone command-line tool for cloning repos and the script that emailed results were both removed, so cloning must now happen through the main workflow and results are no longer emailed automatically.

ai.title: Fix image banner flash on Ctrl+V text paste
ai.summary: Chat keyboard dispatcher now checks clipboard content synchronously before routing paste actions. Ctrl+V triggers a generic paste action that prioritizes image detection; if no image exists, text is inserted immediately. This prevents the brief appearance of the image placeholder banner when pasting text. Changes affect cli/src/chat.tsx, cli/src/hooks/use-chat-keyboard.ts, and cli/src/utils/keyboard-actions.ts.

eli5.text: Here's what happens now: When you press Ctrl+V to paste something into the chat, the app first quickly checks what's actually in your clipboard. If there's an image, it shows the image placeholder banner right away so it can process the picture. But if your clipboard only has text, that image placeholder banner pops up for a split second and then immediately disappears as your text gets inserted, this brief flicker is now fixed. Previously, the app always showed the image banner first and then had to go back and remove it if no image was found, but now it checks first and skips the whole image path entirely when only text is available, so you won't see that flash at all.

eli5.text: The internal evaluation system that tests how well the assistant performs has been updated to use a specific, dated version of the latest Claude model and now runs on a newer version of the underlying tool. The model used for testing is now pinned to a fixed version dated November 1, 2025, which keeps benchmark results consistent instead of relying on a nickname that could point to different versions over time, and this change only affects internal testing, not anything you directly interact with today.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.534 release ships CLI bash context, image support
ai.summary: Version 1.0.534 consolidates a day of CLI and agent improvements into a single release. Bash command context is now unified for the LLM through a `<user_terminal_commands>` block built from `pendingBashMessages`, replacing the split `pendingToolResults` flow. The CLI adds image attachment via /image and clipboard paste with terminal rendering. Best-of-n editors now think before selecting or implementing, with default parallel implementors reduced to 3 (4 in max mode) and a short reason required alongside the `implementationId`. The base2-lite orchestrator variant and base2-editor agent join the lineup, while base2-fast variants are dropped from nightly eval in favor of base2-lite with taskConcurrency lowered to 3.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json hunk bumps version from 1.0.533 to 1.0.534 (single line change in package.json). Release updates list describes shipped user-visible features, model changes, and CLI improvements since 1.0.533.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.534 brings major updates to the command-line assistant, adding native image support and smarter bash command handling. Users can now attach images to conversations via the new /image command or by pasting from the clipboard, with automatic validation and terminal rendering. Bash command results now display instantly in the chat history with a cleaner green-accented look, and background commands update smoothly without screen flicker. The underlying AI models were retuned for faster, more capable responses, with new lightweight agent options for quicker tasks. External benchmarking now supports comparing against Claude and Codex CLI tools, and code search automatically includes hidden configuration directories. Upgrading gives you richer multimodal conversations, faster and more reliable terminal interactions, and consistently better code-suggestions across supported AI providers.

ai.title: Simplify bash command execution API in CLI
ai.summary: Refactors bash command handling in `cli/src/commands/router.ts` to export a simplified `runBashCommand` function. The new API automatically determines ghost vs direct mode based on `streamingAgents` and `isChainInProgress` state, removing the need for explicit options objects. Updates `cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts` to use this new function for immediate command execution when arguments are provided to `/bash`.

eli5.text: When you type a command right after /bash (like /bash ls), the tool now runs it immediately instead of asking you to confirm first. The system automatically handles how the command output appears - it shows as a live updating message during ongoing conversations, or gets added directly to the chat history otherwise. This means you can quickly run bash commands without the extra step of entering a separate mode.

ai.title: Remove unused AgentStep type and SDK imports from evals scaffolding
ai.summary: Removed `AgentStep`, `ToolResultBlockParam`, and `ToolUseBlock` types along with `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` imports from `evals/scaffolding.ts`. The `steps` array in `loopMainPrompt` now uses `any[]` instead of `AgentStep[]`. This cleanup eliminates dead code and unused dependencies in the evals subsystem.

eli5.text: The team cleaned up some leftover building blocks from the evaluation system that were no longer being used. If you peeked at the setup code, you'd see a list that once had strict rules about what could be stored in it now accepts anything, and the unused pieces have been removed entirely. Nothing you can click or see as a user is affected by this. It's just tidy-up work behind the scenes to make the codebase easier to maintain.
